oneLiner: 按端到端的“流程”而非部门职能来设计工作；再造则是推倒重来而非修修补补。
oneLinerEn: Design work around end-to-end processes rather than functions; reengineering means tearing it up, not tidying it.
detail: Hammer 与钱皮(1993)主张对流程做根本再思考、彻底重设计，以在成本、质量、速度上取得飞跃，但高失败率也让“再造”名声复杂。更稳健的日常做法是流程管理:显式描绘价值流、度量周期与缺陷、持续小幅改进。两者共同的盲点常是“人”——流程改了、考核与权责没跟着改，就会反弹。
detailEn: Hammer and Champy (1993) urged fundamental rethinking and radical redesign of processes for leaps in cost, quality and speed — but high failure rates made 'reengineering' a mixed legacy. The steadier daily practice is process management: map the flow, measure cycle time and defects, improve in small steps. The shared blind spot is people — change the process but not the metrics and accountability, and it rebounds.

oneLiner: 计划—执行—检查—处置，把改进变成不断转圈的小步实验。
oneLinerEn: Plan-Do-Check-Act: turn improvement into small experiments that keep cycling.
detail: 由休哈特提出、戴明在日本推广(故又称戴明环)。先假设成因与对策，小范围试行，用数据检查效果，有效则标准化、无效则回到计划再转一圈。它的精神是“用数据代替拍脑袋、用小步迭代代替大规划”，是精益、六西格玛、持续改进的共同底层节律。
detailEn: Propounded by Shewhart and popularised in Japan by Deming (hence the Deming wheel). Hypothesise a cause and countermeasure, run it small, check the effect with data, standardise what works, otherwise return to plan and spin again. Its spirit — data over guesswork, iteration over grand plans — is the shared beat under lean, Six Sigma and kaizen.

oneLiner: 质量是全员、全过程的责任：以客户为中心、持续改进、用统计说话。
oneLinerEn: Quality is everyone's job across the whole process: customer-focused, continually improved, argued with statistics.
detail: 戴明、朱兰、费根堡姆把战后日本制造推向世界之巅的哲学:预防优于检验、管理层的责任大于一线、85% 的质量问题源于系统而非工人。它催生了 ISO 9000 与各类质量奖。落地失败常因把它当运动式口号——缺少长期投入与真正的授权时，全员质量就变成全员填表。
detailEn: Deming, Juran and Feigenbaum carried post-war Japanese manufacturing to the top: prevention over inspection, management bearing more responsibility than the floor, and most defects rooted in the system, not the worker. It begat ISO 9000 and the quality awards. Failed roll-outs treat it as a campaign — without lasting investment and real delegation, 'total quality' decays into 'total form-filling'.

oneLiner: 用 DMAIC 把缺陷压到百万分之三点四级别——靠数据与流程变异，而非灵光一现。
oneLinerEn: Use DMAIC to drive defects toward 3.4 per million — through data and variation, not flashes of insight.
detail: 摩托罗拉成形、通用电气发扬。DMAIC:界定问题、测量现状、分析根因、改进流程、控制成果，每个环节都要求统计证据，并以“绿带/黑带”培养骨干。它擅长在有稳定数据、重复发生的流程上削减变异；相对地，对高度模糊、以创意为主的工作就水土不服。
detailEn: Forged at Motorola, scaled at GE. DMAIC — Define, Measure, Analyse, Improve, Control — demands statistical evidence at every step and builds a cadre of green and black belts. It excels at cutting variation in data-rich, repeating processes and struggles with vague, creative work.

oneLiner: 大野耐一列出七类不创造客户价值的浪费，逐一识别并消除。
oneLinerEn: Ohno named seven wastes that add no customer value; spot and remove each.
detail: 丰田生产方式的两大支柱是“准时化(JIT)”与“自働化”(带人字旁的自动化，异常即停)。大野耐一归纳的七种浪费:过度生产(常被视为万恶之源)、等待、搬运、过度加工、库存、动作、缺陷返工。精益把“消除浪费、持续改善(kaizen)”当作日常纪律，后来溢出到软件、医疗、服务，成为“精益创业”的母体。
detailEn: The Toyota Production System rests on two pillars — just-in-time and jidoka (automation with a human touch: stop when something is wrong). Taiichi Ohno listed seven wastes: overproduction (the root of much else), waiting, transport, over-processing, inventory, motion and defects. Lean turns removing waste and kaizen into daily discipline, later spilling into software, healthcare and services as the parent of the lean startup.

termEn: Theory of Constraints: Mind the Bottleneck
oneLiner: 系统的产出由最慢的那一环决定——优化非瓶颈，多半是自我安慰。
oneLinerEn: Output is set by the slowest link; optimising a non-bottleneck is largely self-soothing.
detail: 高德拉特在《目标》(1984) 里用五步聚焦法:识别系统约束、让一切服从约束、挖尽约束的产能、给约束扩容、然后回到第一步(约束会转移)。它用“有效产出、库存、运营费”三个指标取代局部效率，提醒管理者:链条的强度只看最弱一环，全局改善要从瓶颈下手。
detailEn: Goldratt's The Goal (1984) gives the five focusing steps: identify the constraint, subordinate everything to it, exploit its capacity, elevate it, then repeat as the constraint moves. It measures progress through throughput, inventory and operating expense rather than local efficiency, reminding managers that a chain is only as strong as its weakest link.

oneLiner: 在需要的时间、按需要的量送到——用 EOQ 与看板把库存与缺货在两端之间权衡。
oneLinerEn: Deliver what is needed when it is needed — trade stock against shortages with EOQ and kanban.
detail: 库存既缓冲不确定性也占用资金、掩盖问题(“水位降下,礁石露出”)。经济订货量(EOQ)在订货成本与持有成本间求平衡点;安全库存应对需求与交期的波动;看板则用“下游拉动上游”的信号取代提前生产。JIT 把这套推向极致,但也让系统更脆——一次断供就能停线,需要与供应商深度协同。
detailEn: Inventory buffers uncertainty yet ties up cash and hides problems ('when the water drops, the rocks appear'). EOQ balances ordering against holding cost, safety stock absorbs swings in demand and lead time, and kanban replaces forecast-push with downstream pulling upstream. JIT takes this to the limit but makes the system more brittle — one missed delivery stops the line — demanding close supplier partnership.

oneLiner: 用横条把任务排在时间轴上,一眼看清谁在何时做、进度落在哪里。
oneLinerEn: Lay tasks as bars on a timeline — who does what when, and how far along.
detail: 亨利·甘特在一战前后把这种进度图推广开来。它直观、易沟通,至今仍是项目计划的通用语言。局限是:只画时间不画依赖,复杂项目里“改一条、崩一片”的连锁它表达不出,常需与关键路径、里程碑和燃尽图配合;过度精细的甘特也会沦为“计划剧场”。
detailEn: Henry Gantt popularised the view around the First World War. It is intuitive and communicative and remains the common tongue of project plans. Its limit: it draws time, not dependency, so the knock-on of changing one task in a complex web is invisible — pair it with critical path, milestones and burn-down charts, and beware the over-detailed chart that becomes theatre.

oneLiner: 项目最短工期由最长的依赖任务链决定——这条链上的任务没有缓冲。
oneLinerEn: The shortest possible duration equals the longest dependent chain; tasks on it have no slack.
detail: 把任务按前后依赖连成网络,算出最早/最晚开工时间,总时差为零的那条就是关键路径。它告诉你:盯住关键路径、把资源从富余任务挪去补它,才能缩短工期;而非“哪条看着忙帮哪条”。结合 PERT 还能用乐观/最可能/悲观三点估计不确定性。
detailEn: Link tasks into a dependency network, compute earliest and latest starts, and the zero-float chain is the critical path. It tells you to shorten duration by watching that path and pulling resources from slack tasks to it — not to help whichever task looks busiest. With PERT, three-point estimates add uncertainty.

oneLiner: 把工作量可视化、限制在制品、只在有容量时才拉动——少并行、快流动。
oneLinerEn: Visualise the work, cap work in progress, pull only when there is capacity — less multitasking, faster flow.
detail: 看板源于丰田的补货卡片,经软件领域发展为“列—卡—限额”的方法:用“待办/进行中/已完成”列暴露拥堵,用在制品(WIP)上限迫使团队把手上的事做完再开工新的。核心洞见是:瓶颈时缩短队列、限制并行,比提高每个环节的利用率更能提升整体流动。
detailEn: Kanban grew from Toyota's replenishment cards into a columns-cards-limits method in software: 'To Do / Doing / Done' exposes where work jams, and work-in-progress limits force finishing before starting. The insight is that shortening queues and capping multitasking lifts flow more than pushing each step's utilisation higher.

oneLiner: 让操作工也参与保养设备，追求零故障、零停机、零缺陷。
oneLinerEn: Involve operators in maintaining equipment, aiming for zero breakdowns, downtime and defects.
detail: 源自日本的 TPM 把“维护是维修部门的事”改为全员生产维护：自主保养、计划保养、个别改善、教育培训等八大支柱，让一线员工负责日常点检与清洁，把设备综合效率(OEE)作为核心指标。它与精益、六西格玛互补——精益管流动，TPM 管设备这一环的可靠。
detailEn: Born in Japan, TPM shifts maintenance from 'the repair crew's job' to everyone: eight pillars including autonomous and planned maintenance, focused improvement and training, with operators doing daily checks and cleaning, and overall equipment effectiveness (OEE) as the key metric. It complements lean and Six Sigma — lean manages flow, TPM manages the reliability of the equipment link.

oneLiner: 把供应商到客户的整条链当作一个系统来协调——牛鞭效应是它的经典病症。
oneLinerEn: Manage the supplier-to-customer chain as one system — the bullwhip effect is its classic ailment.
detail: 供应链管理跨企业协调采购、生产、仓储、物流与信息流，目标是以对的量、在对的时间到对的地方。牛鞭效应揭示：需求信号沿链上溯被逐级放大，因过度预测、批量订货与恐慌囤货而失真。解法是共享实时数据、缩短提前期、供应商管理库存(VMI)与延迟策略。
detailEn: Supply-chain management coordinates sourcing, production, warehousing, logistics and information across firms, aiming to get the right quantity to the right place at the right time. The bullwhip effect shows demand signals amplified stage by stage upstream through over-forecasting, batch ordering and panic hoarding. Fixes include sharing real-time data, shortening lead times, vendor-managed inventory and postponement.

oneLiner: 整理、整顿、清扫、清洁、素养——先管好工位，再谈改善文化。
oneLinerEn: Sort, set in order, shine, standardise, sustain — tidy the workplace before chasing a culture of improvement.
detail: 5S 源自丰田，是精益最基础的入门纪律：清除不要之物(整理)、每样东西有固定位置(整顿)、保持干净并暴露异常(清扫)、把前三者制度化(清洁)、靠习惯与自律维持(素养)。看似“大扫除”，实则是让问题一眼可见、减少寻找与浪费的地基，也是检验团队能否坚持小纪律的试金石。
detailEn: 5S, from Toyota, is lean's most basic discipline: clear what is unneeded (Sort), give everything a home (Set in order), keep it clean so faults show (Shine), make the first three the rule (Standardise), hold it by habit (Sustain). It looks like housekeeping but is really the base that makes problems visible and cuts searching and waste — and a litmus test of whether a team can keep small disciplines.

oneLiner: 用物理或流程设计让错误根本犯不出来，而不是靠人加倍小心。
oneLinerEn: Design the product or process so mistakes cannot be made, rather than asking people to be more careful.
detail: 新乡重夫提出的“防呆”：通过接触、固定数量、动作步骤等方式，让零件装反就装不进、少一步就开不了机。它把质量从“事后检验、依赖注意力”转为“源头杜绝”，成本极低却极有效，从 USB-C 可正反插到工厂治具都是它。与 5Why 呼应：与其责人，不如改设计。
detailEn: Shigeo Shingo's 'mistake-proofing': by contact, fixed-count or motion-step devices, a part that is reversed simply will not fit, a skipped step stops the machine. It moves quality from after-the-fact inspection reliant on attention to prevention at source — cheap and powerful, from reversible USB-C connectors to factory jigs. It echoes the 5 Whys: fix the design rather than blame the person.
